objective: T-20260929-72: does the SEC fails-to-deliver balance (FTDSH = fails/shares, FTDADV = fails x price / 21d dollar ADV, high = lower return) rank next-open returns in the ADV top-1500 pool (price >= 5) in 2024+ and 2019+, PIT-lagged by SEC publication? Only if the cheap IC gate passes are 4 preregistered avoid / short books screened.

sources.core_claim: SEC FTD files are pipe-delimited half-month files (a: first half posted at month end; b: about the 15th of the next month) listing every security with a non-zero balance since 2008-09-16; the price field is the previous day close; the SEC says fails arise on long and short sales and are not evidence of naked shorting.
sources.project_applicability: Defines the files, the fields, the publication schedule and the SEC's own caveat; drives the PIT rule and the absent-means-zero rule.
sources.reflection: Page extract via WebFetch summariser (raw curl was rate-limited with HTTP 403); the extract preserves the field list and the quoted caveat.

sources.core_claim: Reg SHO threshold security: aggregate fail-to-deliver position at NSCC for five consecutive settlement days of 10,000 shares or more equal to at least 0.5% of shares outstanding; the FTDSH signal (fails / shares outstanding) is a continuous version of that ratio.
sources.project_applicability: Justifies the fails/shares ratio (FTDSH) as the continuous form of the threshold rule.
sources.reflection: Definition page; says nothing about returns.

sources.core_claim: Stratmann and Welborn (J. Empirical Finance 2016): stocks with fails-to-deliver experience negative abnormal returns proportional to their FTD levels (event study and Fama-French portfolio analysis); short sellers of low and high FTD stocks obtain positive estimated profits net of proprietary borrow costs; FTDs reflect nonbinding short sale constraints.
sources.project_applicability: Origin of the preregistered sign; no effect size taken.
sources.reflection: Abstract page only (full text paywalled); sample period, horizon and effect size not read; period of the study predates 2019 and uses proprietary borrow-cost data we do not have.

sources.core_claim: Autore, Boulton and Braga-Alves (Financial Review 2015): stocks reaching threshold levels of failures become significantly overvalued, with reversals where short-sale constraints bind, but the mispricing is likely difficult to arbitrage because of extreme shorting costs.
sources.project_applicability: Second published support for high FTD -> later reversal, with the warning that the mispricing is costly to short; motivates the ADV top-1500 / price >= 5 pool and the 3%/yr borrow.
sources.reflection: Abstract page only; threshold-list stocks (a tail of FTD), pre-2015 sample; effect size not read. Supports the sign (high FTD -> lower later return) and the shortability warning.

sources.core_claim: Boni (J. Financial Markets 2006): using the cross-section of US equities, evidence consistent with market makers strategically failing to deliver when borrowing costs are high.
sources.project_applicability: Explains why high FTD skews to hard-to-borrow names (search summary only).
sources.reflection: Publisher page not opened (403); search-result abstract only, claim_only, no number used.

sources.core_claim: A 2025 SEC petition file cites a draft Welborn (2025) analysis of Reg SHO threshold lists and NSCC FTD data 2005-2024; the search summary says exchange threshold lists are incomplete while NSCC FTD data are complete.
sources.project_applicability: Most recent lead on FTD data quality; no numbers used.
sources.reflection: PDF fetched but not readable through the tool; claim_only.

sources.core_claim: SEC Office of Economic Analysis memo (2008) on fails to deliver in threshold securities.
sources.reflection: PDF binary not extractable; claim_only, no number used.

sources.core_claim: SEC Office of Economic Analysis study of fails to deliver pre- and post-Regulation SHO (2006).
sources.reflection: PDF binary not extractable; claim_only, no number used.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: Literature says high-FTD mispricing is hard to arbitrage because of shorting costs, so books exist only if a cross-sectional IC survives on 2024+ and the short leg is confined to liquid names.
